Previous feed-forward approaches adopt pixel-aligned Gaussians, coupling splats to image grids. Such alignments are computationally heavy, misaligned with true 3D neighborhoods, and prone to over-densifying smooth areas while under-representing detailed or occluded regions. To ensure refinement respects 3D geometry, we convert pixel-aligned Gaussians to point-based Gaussians and project correspondent pretrained features by camera. In addition, we use window attention to model local relationships of 3D gaussians efficiently. For training, we adopt the architecture from as initializer but remove voxelization.
